title: Trace comparison for a finite flat morphism of smooth curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme equipped with a smooth morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of relative dimension one, and let $f:X\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ that is finite and flat. Here $\mathbf P^1_k$ is the standard projective line of [def-sc-p1-standard]. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ (respectively $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $\mathbf P^1_k$), write $\Omega^1_{A/k}$ (respectively $\Omega^1_{R/k}$) for the $A$-module (respectively $R$-module) generated by symbols $da$ (respectively $dr$), subject to $d(a+a')=da+da'$, $d(aa')=a\,da'+a'\,da$, and $dk=0$; these modules glue to the relative Kähler differential sheaves $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ and $\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}$. Then there exists an $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-linear morphism $\tau:f_*\Omega^1_{X/k}\to\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}$ such that the $f_*\mathcal O_X$-linear comparison map $$f_*\Omega^1_{X/k}\longrightarrow\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}}(f_*\mathcal O_X,\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}),\qquad \omega\longmapsto\bigl(a\longmapsto\tau(a\omega)\bigr)$$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $Y=\mathbf P^1_k$, $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $h=g\circ f$. The standard projective line is projective over $k$, so [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes $g$ proper. Since $f$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] makes $f$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $h$ proper. A field is Noetherian; $g$ and $h$ are of finite type because they are proper, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes both $Y$ and $X$ Noetherian. The affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$, $\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ of [def-sc-p1-standard] show $g$ is smooth of relative dimension one in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], while smoothness of $h$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BRT and 0ATX, proper and Noetherian hypotheses checked for the application

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-proper-curve-dualizing] to $g$ and $h$: $g^!k\cong\Omega^1_{Y/k}[1]$ and $h^!k\cong\Omega^1_{X/k}[1]$. Apply [lem-sc-proper-upper-shriek-composition] to $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow g\operatorname{Spec}k$: $f^!(g^!k)\cong h^!k$. As a derived right adjoint $f^!$ commutes with shifts, so cancelling $[1]$ gives an isomorphism $\alpha:f^!\Omega^1_{Y/k}\cong\Omega^1_{X/k}$. This is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules because the right side is concentrated in degree zero.

source.place: Tags 0BRT and 0ATX, transitivity of dualizing complexes

proof.text: The $n=1$ clause of [lem-pc-projective-space-canonical] says $\Omega^1_{Y/k}$ is invertible. Apply [lem-sc-finite-flat-duality-evaluation] with $L=\Omega^1_{Y/k}$ and transfer its isomorphism through $f_*\alpha^{-1}$ from Step 2. This yields an $f_*\mathcal O_X$-linear isomorphism $\Phi:f_*\Omega^1_{X/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,\Omega^1_{Y/k})$.

source.place: Tags 0BVI and 0FKW, finite duality with an invertible target

proof.text: Define $\tau(\omega)=\Phi(\omega)(1)$. Evaluation at $1$ is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear, so $\tau$ is a morphism of the asserted sheaves. The final clause of [lem-sc-finite-flat-duality-evaluation], or $f_*\mathcal O_X$-linearity of $\Phi$, gives $\Phi(\omega)(a)=\Phi(a\omega)(1)=\tau(a\omega)$ on every open. Thus the comparison map displayed in the statement is exactly $\Phi$, which is an isomorphism by Step 3.
